summary.headline: Suzlon delivered a record 830 MW in Q4 FY26 and 2,456 MW for the year, with FY26 revenue up 54% to INR16,679 crore.
summary.overview: Suzlon reported record Q4 FY26 India deliveries of 830 MW and FY26 deliveries of 2,456 MW (up 58%). Consolidated Q4 revenue was INR5,468 crore with EBITDA of INR964 crore (up 39% YoY) and reported PAT of INR1,114 crore, while FY26 PAT of INR3,153 crore includes a INR742 crore deferred tax asset recognition. Management highlighted a shift toward EPC and development (DevCo) contracts, with EPC share of the order book rising to 28% from about 20% in Q2, and a 2.1 GW Andhra Pradesh development right extended by 24 months. Order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW at the start of the year, while commissioning reached 332 MW in Q4 and 744 MW for the year, with 971 MW erected but not yet commissioned.

financial_highlights.change: Record for any quarter in India; Q4 FY25 was 573 MW (about +45%)

financial_highlights.value: INR833 crore PBT; INR1,114 crore PAT
INR2,422 crore PBT; INR3,153 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PBT +67% YoY; PAT includes INR742 crore deferred tax asset recognition

segments.name: WTG (wind turbine generators)
segments.commentary: FY26 WTG revenue INR14,040 crore (+65% YoY) at 24.5% contribution margin. Management said WTG margins should not materially decline in FY27.

segments.name: Forging & Foundry (SE Forge)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR597 crore (+22% YoY) and EBITDA INR119 crore (+61% YoY), driven by domestic demand and exports.

segments.name: O&M services (OMS)
segments.commentary: Under management is 15.7+ GW in India with machine availability consistently above 95%. Management said the Q2 OMS EBITDA dip was a one-off that has been recouped by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Indian wind installations (industry view): about 8 GW in FY27 and about 10 GW in FY28, with 15 GW around FY30-31. Management said FY27 could be 8-9 GW.
EPC share of order book targeted to rise to 50% by FY28, from 28% now; management expects it to keep growing in FY27.
Management expects EPC order closures to be announced from June 2026 onward; no downward trend in order inflow for a couple of quarters.
Capex run rate of about INR600 crore (plus or minus INR50 crore) going forward, versus about INR550 crore in FY26.
Management did not give absolute FY27 delivery guidance; it pointed to the FY24-FY26 trend (700 MW, 1,550 MW, 2,456 MW) as the indicator.
Unrecognised deferred tax assets estimated at INR3,000-3,500 crore; only deferred tax charge (non-cash) expected in P&L for the next two years.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity of 4.5 GW is fully operational, with 3 AI-enabled smart blade factories being added.
Commissioned 744 MW in FY26 and 332 MW in Q4; 971 MW erected but not commissioned, of which about 350 MW is ready and waiting on customer-side scope.

Andhra Pradesh: PIA extended by 24 months (April 2026), giving 2.1 GW development rights; 775 MW has a PPA being converted to FDRE pending APERC tariff approval, and the remaining 1,325 MW is to be converted into EPC contracts from June over the next 6 months.
DevCo pipeline: 22-23 GW of identified sites, about 8 GW under active development; about 25 GW of land/sites overall, of which 8-10 GW is well advanced.
DevCo capital deployed is about INR300-350 crore against an earlier INR300 crore internal threshold; more working capital may be needed for connectivity and RE parks.
demand_pricing: Order book of 5.9 GW, of which 66% is C&I and PSU; opening FY26 book was 5.0 GW. Management said a Sunsure order was received after the quarter.
S144 order intake is close to 9 GW. New Blue Sky platform (S175 and S163 turbines) launched in Spain to re-enter European and export markets.
PSU demand: NTPC Green is moving from split BOP and WTG contracts to turnkey EPC, with mentions of a 215 MW AP contract and further 540 MW and 2,000 MW AP tranches.

Working capital build is mainly receivables from PSU contracts; management said this was priced into tenders and most is funded through non-fund-based limits. Cash position improved by INR400 crore-plus.
Foreign currency: some contracts carry pass-through clauses; steel is largely pass-through except some PSU contracts. Newer contracts will be priced at prevailing exchange rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will order inflow decline for a few quarters in FY27, given muted Q4 orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW opening. The shift to EPC contracts takes longer to close, but EPC closures are expected to be announced from June.

qa_highlights.question: Can Suzlon help clients manage risk if the wind DSM (deviation settlement) rules tighten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CERC moved wind DSM bands from plus or minus 15% to plus or minus 10%. Suzlon is testing a scheduling and forecasting model at plus or minus 10% and plans to offer it as a paid service, including to existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any non-moving orders in the 5,892 MW backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are currently no non-moving or slow-moving orders in the backlog.

qa_highlights.question: What drives FY27 deliveries, and is about 2,500 MW the most likely outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, pointing to leading indicators and the FY24-26 trend (700 MW, 1,550 MW, 2,456 MW) instead.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for price hikes to protect margins given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said WTG margins should not materially decline, citing pass-through clauses and cost management. Management said pricing on new contracts would reflect current exchange rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the Andhra Pradesh FDRE project and the DevCo model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 775 MW will be converted to FDRE under a PPA, with clients possibly taking over the PPA and Suzlon supplying full FDRE. The remaining 1,325 MW will be converted into turnkey EPC contracts from June.

risks_watch: Execution: 971 MW erected but not commissioned, with about 350 MW waiting on customer-side readiness; commissioning pace and receivables recovery need tracking.
Working capital and receivables from PSU contracts; operating cash flow of about INR12 billion versus EBITDA of INR30 billion in FY26.
Possible DSM tightening (plus or minus 10%) and stay status, which may affect wind project economics.
EPC conversion timing: the 1,325 MW AP conversion and EPC contract announcements are expected from June; the 775 MW FDRE PPA depends on APERC tariff approval and client takeover.
Commodity and currency exposure on non-pass-through contracts; management gave no quantified margin guidance beyond WTG margins not materially declining.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on deliveries, commissioning and the EPC/DevCo transition, with management pointing to the FY26 commitments delivered. Evasive on specific FY27 delivery and order numbers, which they declined to give, and on monthly installation disclosure, which they said they would evaluate internally.
key_quotes: Suzlon delivered a record 830 megawatts in Q4 and 2,456 megawatts in FY '26, which are our ever-highest deliveries in India.
Our net cash balance at INR2,384 crores further enhances our financial flexibility and resilience.
WTG margins, I don't think materially can go down.
We will provide the right from land to the entire project commissioning on EPC on a turnkey basis.

adds.what: 3 AI-enabled smart blade factories being added (manufacturing base of 4.5 GW fully operational)
Andhra Pradesh development rights 2.1 GW (PIA extended 24 months); 775 MW PPA being converted to FDRE pending APERC approval, 1,325 MW to be converted into EPC
DevCo pipeline: 22-23 GW identified sites, about 8 GW under active development

growth.why: No absolute FY27 delivery guidance; management points to FY26 trend (2,456 MW) and industry installs of ~8 GW in FY27, backed by a 5.9 GW order book (up from 5.0 GW), 332 MW Q4 commissioning and a 2.1 GW AP development right, while capex is raised to ~INR600 crore run-rate.
